newsitem.title: USA: Tanker flips, burns by Miami airport, closing runway.
newsitem.headline: Tanker flips, burns by Miami airport, closing runway.

text.p: An oil tanker flipped over on a road near the Miami International Airport Friday, about a mile from the site of a fatal air crash the previous day, igniting a blaze and forcing airport authorities to close a runway.
The driver was pulled from the cab, witnesses said, but his condition was not known.
The tanker erupted into a fireball as soon as it overturned, one witness said. Flames spread for a few hundred yards (meters), setting ablaze trees and bushes on the airport perimeter.

A thick cloud of black smoke billowed into the sky. Airport spokesman Mark Henderson said one runway had been closed because the smoke was affecting visibility. He could not say how many flights were disturbed.
Fire rescue teams poured a blizzard of foam onto the inferno and extinguished the blaze around the tanker in about fifteen minutes, but roadside fires continued to burn.

The only building in the vicinty is a restaurant and firefighters immediately evacuated it. "We protected the restaurant and attacked the fire from there," Metro-Dade Fire Rescue spokesman Keith Bowermaster said.
The accident occurred on the south side of the airport about a mile from where a cargo plane crashed on take-off on Thursday, killing four people.

A news conference by police and National Transportation Safety Board officials was taking place at the plane crash site when the tanker accident occurred. The smoke appeared in the background of TV crews at the news conference.
Roads at both crash sites were closed, causing traffic chaos.
